options.description: Each task is a short script of owner messages (build it, then change a rule, then add a feature). The score counts both the hidden acceptance checks the code passes and plumb's own trail: records captured, questions raised, gates passed, links left stale. This stresses the parts of plumb that matter (intent changes, supersedes, proof), at the cost of a few more turns.
options.label: The loop, scripted requests (Recommended)

options.description: One message per task; the score is only the hidden acceptance checks the code passes. Cheapest, but it barely exercises plumb beyond the first capture.
options.label: Code only, one request

options.description: A --one-shot flag runs the single-request form, the default runs the scripted form. More to build and maintain.
options.label: Both, chosen by a flag

payload.question: What should the benchmark measure: how far a cheap model gets through plumb's whole loop on a scripted sequence of owner requests, or only the code it ships from one request?
